newsitem.title: USA: Bondholder atty steps back from Marvel accusation.
newsitem.headline: Bondholder atty steps back from Marvel accusation.

text.p: An attorney representing the bondholders of Marvel Entertainment Group Inc's parent company stepped back from allegations that a Marvel reorganization plan was an inside deal, a legal source said.
But the attorney, David Friedman, told Reuters the allegations were irrelevant to the current motion to remove an automatic stay.
"I am not going to attempt to prove fraud in the context of this motion only because it's unecessary...," Friedman said.

Friedman referred to the hearing on a bondholder request to lift an automatic stay that would allow them to foreclose on common stock that backs their bonds. Testimony was completed on Tuesday, Marvel Entertainment spokesman Michael Freitag said, and Bankruptcy Judge Helen Balick was expected to render a decision after 1615 EST/2115 GMT.

Freitag said the judge indicated there was no evidence fraud was perpetrated by Marvel. Bondholders alleged the reorganization plan, put forth by Ronald Perelman to reimburse them $0.045 on the dollar in exchange for the shares collateralizing the debt, was "an inside deal" intended to "deceive the court."
